newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore diesel up on crude, possible IOC demand.
newsitem.headline: Singapore diesel up on crude, possible IOC demand.

text.p: Singapore oil products prices rose slightly on Friday on firmer crude prices with gas oil boosted by expectations of a higher award by India for December arrival, traders said.
Gas oil prices firmed on higher swap values and higher physical bids on some traders' expectations that Indian Oil Corp may award up to 600,000-tonnes in its December purchase tender.

Earlier the market was expecting India to award around 300,000 to 400,000 but some traders revised their ideas upward and bought the swaps, traders said. November gas oil swaps traded to a high of 30.20, up 25 cents from Thursday.
Traders said the talks of IOC buying more comes despite the shutdown of two jetties at Kandla, India's largest oil port.
On the physical market one trader was bidding for 150,000 barrel loading November 9-13 at $30.00 fob, up 30 cents from Thursday's traded level.

The jet fuel market remains depressed with reports of high stocks in Japan which for the first time in 17 months had surpassed levels a year earlier. Stocks for September were at 4.76 million kilolitres.
As a result, the gas oil/jet fuel spread for December crunched between 85 cents and $1.05.
Several gasoline buyers were seen for 92 octane unleaded cargoes with bids ranging at between $24.00 to 24.10. Bids were also seen for 95 octane at $24.80 and for 97 octane at $26.15, all fon basis.
A cargo of 97-octane unleaded gasoline lifting November 19-24 was offered at $26.45 per barrel fob Singapore, up 5 cents from Thursday's deal level.

Naphtha firmed with November swaps quoted at $22.05/22.10, up from Thursday's $21.90/22.10. A South Korean trader was heard seeking a cargo lifting from Singapore mid-November but refiners said supplies were and tight. --Singapore Newsroom (+65-8703093)
